lines.en: scene black
The following commentary centers around a scene that is not meant to be explicitly understood.
lines.zh: 以下解说围绕一个本就不该被明确理解的场景。

lines.en: Please be advised that proceeding from this point on may negatively impact your perspective of Il Cervo if the underlying mysticism of it added to your experience as a reader.
lines.zh: 请知悉，如果《Il Cervo》背后的神秘主义为你的阅读体验加了分，那么从这里继续下去可能会损害你对它的看法。

lines.en: This commentary exists to document and showcase different aspects of my creative process, and {b}will{/i} contain direct spoilers on what {i}some{/i} of the event means.
lines.zh: 本解说的存在是为了记录并展示我创作过程的不同侧面，{b}并且会{/i}直接剧透这个事件{i}某些{/i}部分的含义。

lines.en: Additionally, please do not share any of this information with readers who would rather {i}not{/i} know — as I do not want their experience to be altered in any form.
lines.zh: 此外，请不要把这些信息分享给那些{i}宁可不{/i}知道的读者——因为我不希望他们的体验以任何形式被改变。

lines.en: Please exit the commentary now if you would rather remain in the dark.
lines.zh: 如果你宁愿蒙在鼓里，现在请退出解说。

lines.en: scene ilcervo1 with dissolve2
Hello — and welcome to the scene commentary on “Il Cervo.”
lines.zh: 你好——欢迎来到《Il Cervo》的场景解说。

lines.en: I am your host — a deer that knows too much.
lines.zh: 我是你们的主持人——一只知道得太多的鹿。

lines.en: Selebus is locked in his room right now, so he has tasked me with explaining to you some of the many mysteries this event has to offer.
lines.zh: Selebus 现在把自己锁在房间里，所以他把向你解释这个事件众多谜团中一部分的任务交给了我。

lines.en: I will attempt to do this in a way that does not reveal any information that could not already be gleaned by someone with a heightened sense of self, but be warned-
lines.zh: 我会尽量用一种不泄露任何「自我意识敏锐的人本就能自行领会」之外信息的方式来做这件事，但请听我警告——

lines.en: You {i}will{/i} walk away from here closer to enlightenment. And you {i}will{/i} learn things about a world you’ll never live in that you might wish you’d never learned at all.
lines.zh: 你从这里离开时{i}一定{/i}会更接近觉悟。而你{i}一定{/i}会了解到一个你永远不会生活在其中的世界的种种，而那些东西你也许会希望自己从未了解过。

lines.en: Il Cervo does not exist.
lines.zh: 《Il Cervo》并不存在。

lines.en: scene ilcervo2 with flash
In fact, there are {i}many{/i} scenes in Lessons in Love that do not exist — even within the fragmented and broken context of its “reality.”
lines.zh: 事实上，《Lessons in Love》里有{i}很多{/i}场景并不存在——哪怕是在它那个支离破碎的「现实」语境之内。

lines.en: There are things the reader sees that no one else does. Things that attempt to bridge the gap between what is real and what is not, but get mixed up and confused along the way.
lines.zh: 有些东西只有读者看得到，别人都看不到。它们试图在真实与不真实之间架起桥梁，却在过程中被搅乱、混淆。

lines.en: And these moments, while they may contain information imperative to understanding some aspects of the story, do not {i}need{/i} to be understood for they exist in a suspended realm of the make-believe.
lines.zh: 而这些时刻，虽然可能包含理解故事某些方面所必需的信息，却{i}并不{/i}需要被理解，因为它们存在于一个悬置的虚构领域里。

lines.en: These moments, while they may be caused by different things, are sometimes the convergence of multiple minds melted down into a thick soup before being mixed with oil and water and everything else that won’t work.
lines.zh: 这些时刻虽然可能由不同的事物引起，但有时是多个心智汇聚在一起、融成一锅浓汤，再跟油、水以及所有那些混不到一起的东西搅拌起来。

lines.en: In Il Cervo, we see this happening with all four characters present  — and the dreamlike state the event occurs in is merely a result of that.
lines.zh: 在《Il Cervo》里，我们看到四个角色全都在场时发生了这种事——而这个事件所处的梦幻状态只不过是那带来的结果。

lines.en: scene ilcom1
Which is precisely why the idea of understanding it at all is little more than wishful thinking or false interpretation.
lines.zh: 这正是为什么「理解它」这个念头本身不过是痴心妄想或错误解读。

lines.en: You’re playing a losing game — attempting to make sense of what time can not keep up with, all while it rapidly changes based on external forces like who else is present and what you saw on the road today.
lines.zh: 你在玩一场必输的游戏——试图理解连时间都跟不上的东西，而它还在根据外部力量飞速变化，比如还有谁在场、你今天在路上看到了什么。

lines.en: Have you ever thought about what you were thinking about just to think that you are now thinking about what you were thinking about?
lines.zh: 你有没有想过你当时在想什么，只为了想明白你现在正在想你当时在想什么？

lines.en: Or held a mirror close to another mirror to create a pocket dimension that carries on forever?
lines.zh: 或者把一面镜子贴近另一面镜子，造出一个永远延续的袖珍维度？

lines.en: What if you gathered up your friends and you all did that at once? Could you create a black hole with little more than your minds? Could {i}you{/i} earn a gold star?
lines.zh: 如果你把朋友们聚起来、大家一起这么做呢？你能只凭你们的心智造出一个黑洞吗？{i}你{/i}能拿到一颗金星吗？

lines.en: I don’t think this is what Dickinson was talking about when she said the brain is wider than the sky — but maybe, in some world, it is. And maybe this world is that one. Or that one is this one.
lines.zh: 我不觉得狄金森说「大脑比天空更宽广」时讲的是这个——但也许在某个世界里，它确实是。而也许这个世界就是那个世界。或者那个世界就是这个世界。

lines.en: {b}I DIGRESS.{/b}
lines.zh: {b}我跑题了。{/b}

lines.en: scene ilcervo7 with flash
Losing game aside, the mystic and borderline spiritual nature of Il Cervo lands Kaori, Ami, and Sensei in the same place. Just none of them are {i}actually{/i} there.
lines.zh: 先不说必输的游戏，《Il Cervo》那种神秘、近乎灵性的性质把 Kaori、Ami 和 Sensei 带到了同一个地方。只是他们{i}实际上{/i}谁都不在那儿。

lines.en: Or maybe they are and they just can’t see each other. There were never {i}cards{/i} though. Or elves or stars or anything like that. Just a handful of minds and a mind full of hands.
lines.zh: 又或者他们在那儿，只是互相看不见。不过从来就{i}没有牌{/i}。也没有精灵、星星或任何那种东西。只有几个心智，和一个装满了手的心智。

lines.en: scene ilcom2 with flash
Wait hold on I need to talk about atoms.
lines.zh: 等等，我得先说说原子。

lines.en: Surely you’ve heard that thing about how atoms can sort of tunnel into and through each other if they all align at the perfect moment, right?
lines.zh: 你肯定听过那种说法吧：如果所有原子在完美的时刻对齐，它们就能彼此穿隧、互相穿过。

lines.en: It won’t ever {i}actually{/i} happen — but it is scientifically possible.
lines.zh: 它{i}实际{/i}永远不会发生——但在科学上是可能的。

lines.en: scene ilcom3
I wanted to show you by layering different versions of this picture on top of each other a bunch of times, but it doesn’t look as cool as I wanted to. You get the point, though. I hope.
lines.zh: 我本想把这幅图的不同版本一层层叠上很多次来给你演示，但效果没我想要的那么酷。不过你懂意思了吧。我希望如此。

lines.en: But yeah, think of it like that. Think of it like several human consciences and consciousnesses receiving physical entities that combine at a perfect moment that can only be explored by someone with access to them.
lines.zh: 但是啊，就这么想。把它想成好几个人的良知与意识接收到实体，在完美的时刻结合起来，而只有能接触到它们的人才能探索。

lines.en: That someone is Selebus. Not me, I am a deer. But he told me that’s what was happening here.
lines.zh: 那个人就是 Selebus。不是我，我是一只鹿。但他告诉我这里发生的就是这个。

lines.en: scene ilcervo2 with flash
He told me that the reason things seem so fucking wonky and weird is because they are.
lines.zh: 他告诉我，事情之所以看起来他妈那么歪七扭八、那么怪，是因为它们本来就是。

lines.en: It’s because maintaining a coherent thought pattern when several minds are fighting for dominance is, just like the faceless elf game and Il Cervo as a whole, a losing battle.
lines.zh: 因为在好几个心智争夺主导权时还想维持连贯的思路，就跟那个无面精灵游戏、以及整个《Il Cervo》一样，是一场必败之战。

lines.en: So in order to better understand this puzzle, we must first look at the pieces.
lines.zh: 所以为了更好地理解这个谜题，我们得先看看这些碎片。

lines.en: scene ilcom4 with flash
This is Ami. You know her. And she’s having a pretty tough time at this point in the story, so you can make an assumption right off the bat that she isn’t of “sound mind.”
lines.zh: 这是 Ami。你认识她。在故事的这一点上她过得相当艰难，所以你大可以一开始就假设她并非「心智健全」。

lines.en: Important note: she was a player before the scene started.
lines.zh: 重要提示：在场景开始之前，她是个玩家。

lines.en: scene ilcom5
Then there’s Kaori — who has {i}never{/i} really been of “sound mind” at any point in the game. But she {i}too{/i} is facing turmoil right now in the fact that she recently became a mother.
lines.zh: 然后是 Kaori——在游戏里的任何时刻，她{i}从来{/i}算不上「心智健全」。但她{i}也{/i}正在面对动荡，因为她最近当了妈妈。

lines.en: Important note: she is the game master.
lines.zh: 重要提示：她是游戏主持人。

lines.en: scene ilcom6 with flash
Sensei’s there too, of course. And while it’s easy for the reader to go out on a limb and assume that this is just one more example of his mind playing tricks on him, that’s wrong.
lines.zh: Sensei 当然也在。读者很容易大胆假设这不过是他脑子又在骗他的又一个例子，但那是错的。

lines.en: Because again, {i}this isn’t happening.{/i} We’ve just {i}decided{/i} it’s happening because how is anyone supposed to guess that is all just some crazy stream of combined consciousness stuff? Crazy.
lines.zh: 因为再说一次，{i}这事并没有发生。{/i}我们只是{i}决定{/i}它发生了，因为谁能猜到那全都是某种疯狂的心智混合流之类的东西？疯了。

lines.en: Important note: he joined last.
lines.zh: 重要提示：他是最后一个加入的。

lines.en: scene ilcom7 with flash
One last element. One last mind. Again, unnoticed.
lines.zh: 最后一个元素。最后一个心智。再一次，没人注意到。

lines.en: Important note: when did she even get here?
lines.zh: 重要提示：她到底是什么时候到这里的？

lines.en: scene ilcervo8 with flash
Four people, four minds. Now turn them into atoms and stack them on top of each other. Watch them tunnel like worms, not deer (me). Or ants, not deer (you).
lines.zh: 四个人，四个心智。现在把他们变成原子，一层层叠起来。看它们像蠕虫那样穿隧，不是鹿（我）。或者像蚂蚁，不是鹿（你）。

lines.en: When you watch those creatures build, you can comprehend what they’re doing. Right? But you don’t really know {i}why{/i} they’re doing it.
lines.zh: 当你看着那些生物建造时，你能理解它们在做什么。对吧？但你并不真正知道它们{i}为什么{/i}这么做。

lines.en: There’s this tunnel at a zoo I go to full of naked mole rats. They just dig. All day. They’re not going anywhere. They’re just digging. And I think that’s cool. Kind of unrelated though. I’ll stop.
lines.zh: 我常去的那个动物园里有条隧道，里面全是裸鼹鼠。它们就是挖。一整天。它们哪儿也去不了。它们就是挖。我觉得那挺酷的。不过这有点不相关。我不说了。

lines.en: Sensei tells a story about whales that speak in verse. About the formation of the uniVERSE. Not an intentional play on words there. Merely a coincidence.
lines.zh: Sensei 讲了个关于用诗说话、关于宇宙（uniVERSE）形成的故事。那不是在故意玩双关。只是个巧合。

lines.en: But maybe that’s not ACTUALLY what it was about and maybe it was just framed that way?
lines.zh: 但也许它实际上讲的不是那个，也许只是被那样包装了？

lines.en: What else is present that was formed in a peculiar way? What do you know now? And was this {i}his{/i} story just because he was the one telling it?
lines.zh: 还有什么是以一种奇特方式形成、也出现在这里的？你现在知道什么了？而这是不是{i}他的{/i}故事，只因为讲的人是他？

lines.en: Was {i}Ami’s{/i} story Ami’s? The one about fitting in when, at least up until now, she fit in better than everyone else around her?
lines.zh: {i}Ami 的{/i}故事是 Ami 的吗？那个关于融入的故事——而至少到目前为止，她比周围所有人都融得更好？

lines.en: There’s that stuff about deer parts too. About pieces of things that belong to one thing being attached to another thing. THAT part should have been easy to understand at least, right?
lines.zh: 还有那些关于鹿的部件的东西。关于属于一个东西的碎片被接到另一个东西上。那部分至少本该容易理解，对吧？

lines.en: scene ilcom8 with flash
Because right after all that, you see this crazy scar on her body for the first time. And that gets you to think? Woah. What if {i}she{/i} has deer parts? Cool. You got that. I’m proud of you.
lines.zh: 因为就在那之后，你第一次看到她身上那道疯狂的伤疤。而那让你想？哇。万一{i}她{/i}有鹿的部件呢？酷。你懂了。我为你骄傲。

lines.en: scene ilcervo9
{b}BUT NOT PROUD ENOUGH.{/b}
lines.zh: {b}但骄傲得还不够。{/b}

lines.en: scene ilcervo13 with flash
Because Kaori is just one thing. LIGHTNING SYMBOLISM ROUND, GO.
lines.zh: 因为 Kaori 只是一个东西。闪电象征环节，开始。

lines.en: The repeated use of “Dad?” (primarily from Kaori) is that constant nagging fear inside both of them that has contributed to the degradation of their mental states and created this situation to begin with.
lines.zh: 「爸爸？」这句反复出现（主要出自 Kaori），是他们两人心里那种持续纠缠的恐惧，正是它促成了他们精神状态的恶化，并一开始就造就了这个局面。

lines.en: The moon that Kaori sits on is meant to show that she is POWERFUL and RELEVANT — something readers should understand better ala Kittens and what comes before it.
lines.zh: Kaori 坐的那轮月亮意在表明她强大且重要——读者应该能通过《Kittens》及其之前的内容更好地理解这一点。

lines.en: The deer (me) were chosen because they are WEAK and PLENTIFUL and are respected for their beauty by many while being hunted for sport by predators (Sensei) on the other end of the spectrum.
lines.zh: 选鹿（我）是因为它们弱小且数量众多，被许多人因其美丽而尊崇，同时又被另一端的掠食者（Sensei）当作猎物捕杀。

lines.en: And hey! You know what else reproduces like crazy and is hunted by predators?
lines.zh: 而且嘿！你知道还有什么繁殖得疯狂、又被掠食者捕猎吗？

lines.en: The fucking LIONFISH, bro. They straight up destroyed the Florida coastline once because people bought them as pets and just threw out into the ocean where they fucked like wild and killed everything.
lines.zh: 他妈是狮子鱼啊，兄弟。它们曾经直接把佛罗里达海岸线毁了，因为人们把它们买来当宠物，然后随手丢进海里，它们在那儿疯狂交配、杀光一切。

lines.en: Also whales if you’re Captain Ahab. Which are relevant in their own regard because Moby Dick is what popularized the idea of white whales symbolizing endless pursuit.
lines.zh: 如果你是亚哈船长，鲸鱼也算。而鲸鱼本身也有其相关性，因为《白鲸》正是让白鲸象征无尽追逐这一意象流行起来的原因。

lines.en: And we already know that Sensei’s white whale is the idea of being happy. Or falling in love {i}for real.{/i}
lines.zh: 而我们已经知道，Sensei 的白鲸就是「幸福」这个念头。或者说{i}真正{/i}坠入爱河。

lines.en: scene ilcom10 with flash
But what about this thing?
lines.zh: 但这个东西呢？

lines.en: Because Ami’s clearly broken in many different ways, but does {i}her{/i} mind really belong in a thick soup with Kaori’s and Sensei’s?
lines.zh: 因为 Ami 显然以许多不同方式坏掉了，但{i}她{/i}的心智真的该跟 Kaori 和 Sensei 的搅进同一锅浓汤里吗？

lines.en: What does {i}she{/i} want? And is it simple enough to water down to a tiny idea like “being with Sensei” when readers should understand by now that there’s much more to her than meets the eye?
lines.zh: {i}她{/i}想要什么？而当读者现在该明白她远不止表面所见时，她的愿望真能简单到被稀释成「跟 Sensei 在一起」这种小小的念头吗？

lines.en: What is your white whale, Ami? And how can you stay so composed in the throes of a scenario that, like Somnambula, seems so {i}wrong{/i} but is presented in a way that is so {i}calm{/i} and {i}factual?{/i}
lines.zh: 你的白鲸是什么，Ami？而在一场像《Somnambula》那样显得如此{i}不对劲{/i}、却被以如此{i}平静{/i}而{i}就事论事{/i}的方式呈现的境况煎熬之中，你怎么能保持这么镇定？

lines.en: Is it because you like this?
lines.zh: 是因为你喜欢这样吗？

lines.en: Or have you merely just seen it already?
lines.zh: 还是说你只是早就见过了？

lines.en: scene black
scene ilcervo1
Il Cervo does not exist.
lines.zh: 《Il Cervo》并不存在。

lines.en: It’s just like any other dream. The only difference is you got to see four of them at once this time.
lines.zh: 它就跟任何别的梦一样。唯一的区别是这次你一次看到了四个。

lines.en: But of course, that then raises the question — what {i}else{/i} isn’t real?
lines.zh: 但当然，这就引出一个问题——{i}还有{/i}什么不是真的？

lines.en: What {i}else{/i} have you seen that is merely a dream?
lines.zh: 你还看到过{i}别的{/i}什么只是梦的东西？

lines.en: Because the answer’s right there.
lines.zh: 因为答案就在那儿。

lines.en: You just don’t want to believe it.
lines.zh: 你只是不想相信而已。

lines.en: scene meintheroom1 with flash
: Emily has lied to you! The brain’s not wider than the sky! It’s mushy, grayish, pinkish slop! It dies as every day goes by!
lines.zh: : Emily 骗了你！大脑并不比天空宽广！它是糊状的、灰扑扑、粉兮兮的烂泥！每过一天它都在死去！

lines.en: scene meintheroom2
: But what if there was more than one? Could several brains just...work in kind? Transmit to one another how it’s mindless to have just {i}one{/i} mind?
lines.zh: : 但如果不止一个呢？几个大脑能不能就……协同运作？互相传递「只拥有{i}一个{/i}心智是多么无脑」这件事？

lines.en: : Do they know something we don’t know? Have they joined to see our lives condemned? Or can we unlock permanence by just...diving deeper {i}into{/i} them?
lines.zh: : 它们知道我们不知道的什么吗？它们联合起来是为了看着我们的人生被定罪吗？还是说我们只要……{i}潜入{/i}它们更深处，就能解锁永恒？

lines.en: : There are paradoxes all around you...for {i}time{/i} moves in circles too — and it will one day need to start over.
lines.zh: : 你周围到处都是悖论……因为{i}时间{/i}也在绕圈——而它总有一天需要重新开始。

lines.en: : I’ve been trying to think of a good word for when that happens.
lines.zh: : 我一直在想，该给那一刻找个什么好词。

lines.en: : I keep landing on “midnight.”
lines.zh: : 我每次都落到「午夜」。

lines.en: : Anyway, I hope the deer was kind to you. It is at this point that I will be answering questions submitted by the community.
lines.zh: : 总之，希望那只鹿对你温和。现在我要开始回答社区提交的问题了。

lines.en: : Question one — if Lessons in Love were a story you were telling in response to a prompt of two words, what would be the two words that you got that started you telling this story?
lines.zh: : 问题一——如果《Lessons in Love》是你为回应一个两词提示而讲的故事，那么让你开始讲这个故事的那两个词是什么？

lines.en: : Easy. Time and God — which are perhaps the two words with the most profound impact in the way I write as a whole.
lines.zh: : 简单。时间与神——这大概是整体上对我的写作方式影响最深远的两个词。

lines.en: : Religion alone is something that I’ve been writing about since I was a young teenager, but it wasn’t until much later in life that the chronophobia kicked in.
lines.zh: : 单是宗教，我从十几岁起就在写，但直到人生晚得多的时候，时间恐惧症才发作。

lines.en: : Now, those two forces combine to not only create the building blocks for Lessons in Love, but to dictate the way I see the world and guide my creative energy.
lines.zh: : 现在，这两股力量结合起来，不仅构成了《Lessons in Love》的基石，还决定了我看世界的方式、引导着我的创作能量。

lines.en: : Question two — How did the idea to link the event with D'Annunzio's poem come about?
lines.zh: : 问题二——把这个事件跟邓南遮的诗联系起来的想法是怎么来的？

lines.en: : Going into Il Cervo, I knew I wanted to do something dreamlike, but I wasn’t really sure how to start. So I did what I’ve done countless other times and looked up inspiration in the form of poetry.
lines.zh: : 开始做《Il Cervo》时，我知道我想做点梦幻的东西，但不太确定怎么开头。于是我做了无数次做过的事：从诗里寻找灵感。

lines.en: : When I read the poem “Il Cervo,” I was immediately captivated by its almost trance-like nature and normalized brutality interlaced with imagery that, while confusing to me, still painted a vivid picture.
lines.zh: : 读到《Il Cervo》这首诗时，我立刻被它近乎恍惚的性质、以及那种被常态化的残暴所吸引，它们与一些意象交织在一起——那些意象虽然让我困惑，却仍描绘出生动的画面。

lines.en: : Something you may not know about me if you’re a casual player is that I have aphantasia. I am incapable of {i}literally{/i} visualizing things.
lines.zh: : 如果你只是个随便玩玩的玩家，你可能不知道我有心盲症。我{i}字面意义上{/i}无法在脑中成像。

lines.en: : So I have an interesting relationship with imagery as a whole as its mere purpose is directly antihtetical to what I am personally capable of.
lines.zh: : 所以我跟意象整体的关系挺有意思，因为它的存在目的本身就与我个人能做到的事直接相悖。

lines.en: : But that doesn’t mean that I can not read words meant to paint pictures and interpret them in my own way.
lines.zh: : 但那不意味着我读不了那些意在作画、并且我能以自己的方式解读的文字。

lines.en: : So while I might not literally {i}see{/i} what others can, I imagine I can still feel the emotions those paintings of words are designed to evoke.
lines.zh: : 所以虽然我可能无法{i}字面{/i}看到别人能看到的，我想我仍然能感受到那些用文字作的画所要唤起的情感。

lines.en: : That said, the gruesome yet vivid language of Il Cervo immediately struck me as something that would mesh seamlessly with a scene meant to occur between multiple realms of existence.
lines.zh: : 话虽如此，《Il Cervo》那种骇人却生动的语言立刻让我觉得，它会跟一个本该发生在多重存在领域之间的场景无缝契合。

lines.en: : In fact, I think the poem alone can convey the same feelings my event does despite the literal literary natures of them being mostly antonymic.
lines.zh: : 事实上，我觉得单是那首诗就能传达我的事件所传达的同样感受，尽管两者在字面文学性质上大多是反义的。

lines.en: : But even that I find beautiful. And it’s one of my favorite poems in the game now.
lines.zh: : 但连这一点我都觉得美。而且它现在是游戏里我最喜欢的诗之一。

lines.en: : Question three — Was there any story Akira could have told to get a gold star?
lines.zh: : 问题三——Akira 有没有可能讲出某个能拿到金星的故事？

lines.en: : No. Like I mentioned in the commentary, he was playing a losing game. But to further elaborate on that, let me put it this way.
lines.zh: : 没有。就像我在解说里提到的，他玩的是一场必输的游戏。不过要进一步说明，我这么说吧。

lines.en: : There are no two people in this world who think {i}exactly{/i} the same as one another.
lines.zh: : 这个世界上没有两个人的想法{i}完全{/i}一样。

lines.en: : Meaning that, if you were to turn their brains to string (or atoms, like we mentioned before), you’d find that they’d be all knotted up come nightfall.
lines.zh: : 也就是说，如果你把他们的大脑变成线（或者像我们之前说的，原子），你会发现到夜幕降临时它们全都会缠成死结。

lines.en: : This isn’t a {i}bad{/i} thing, though. It just displays a level of permanent incompatibility in terms of the way different creatures perceive different things.
lines.zh: : 不过这不是件{i}坏{/i}事。它只是显示出一种永久的互不兼容——在生物感知事物的方式层面。

lines.en: : And given that Il Cervo is an event where several streams of consciousness combine into one viewable entity, it was always going to be about things not {i}fitting.{/i} Because they can’t.
lines.zh: : 而既然《Il Cervo》是一个多股意识汇成一个可视实体的事件，它注定要讲的就是东西们{i}合不来{/i}。因为它们就是合不来。

lines.en: : Each character had a different puzzle they were trying to solve. And even if those puzzles were similar in nature, they were doomed from the moment they “sat down.”
lines.zh: : 每个角色都有各自想解的谜题。而就算那些谜题性质相似，从他们「坐下」的那一刻起就注定失败。

lines.en: : Question four — Why does Akira and Kaori keep changing the titles of faceless elf and gold star?
lines.zh: : 问题四——为什么 Akira 和 Kaori 老是改无面精灵和金星的标题？

lines.en: : Because they never mattered. The game wasn’t {i}actually{/i} a game — which made the inclusion of rules unnecessary and null.
lines.zh: : 因为它们从来就不重要。那游戏{i}实际上{/i}不是个游戏——这就让规则的加入既没必要也无效。

lines.en: : Question five — Il Cervo is the first time we see Kaori’s scar in-game, but this is something that was already known to people outside of the game due to image requests...
lines.zh: : 问题五——《Il Cervo》是我们第一次在游戏里看到 Kaori 的伤疤，但由于图片请求，游戏外的人早就知道这件事了……

lines.en: : How do you feel about the impact of these reveals being potentially lessened by information from outside of the game?
lines.zh: : 对于这些揭示的冲击力可能因游戏外信息而被削弱，你怎么看？

lines.en: : To be frank, I don’t like it. And I made a mistake in revealing Kaori’s scar {i}years{/i} before I should have, which ultimately led to people using it as fodder for theory-crafting.
lines.zh: : 坦白说，我不喜欢。我在本该揭示的{i}好几年前{/i}就透露了 Kaori 的伤疤，这是个错误，最终导致人们拿它当理论脑补的素材。

lines.en: : {size=-2}It was an amateur move that I made before ever realizing how big this game would get — but it’s one that I’d correct later on with the addition of Imani and the ban on her requests until her respective condition was revealed.{/size}
lines.zh: : {size=-2}那是我还没意识到这游戏会变多大时做的业余举动——但后来我通过加入 Imani、并在她相应的状况被揭示之前禁止相关请求，纠正了这一点。{/size}

lines.en: : But yeah. Knowing what I know now, I definitely would like to go back in time and create a separate model for her older requests that would have changed upon the reveal in Il Cervo.
lines.zh: : 但是啊。以我现在的认知，我绝对想回到过去，为她那些较早的请求单独做一个模型，让它在《Il Cervo》的揭示时发生变化。

lines.en: : Question six — How do you approach events that the community find hard to understand, and if things are intentionally confusing, how do you make that confusion feel like it fits in?
lines.zh: : 问题六——对于那些社区觉得难理解的事件，你是怎么处理的？而如果那些东西是有意让人困惑的，你又怎么让这种困惑显得合理融入？

lines.en: : I feel like Lessons in Love is the type of game where {i}anything{/i} can fit in if I try hard enough. And that’s the exact type of game I’ve wanted to make from the beginning.
lines.zh: : 我觉得《Lessons in Love》是那种只要我够努力、{i}任何东西{/i}都能塞进去的游戏。而这正是我从一开始就想做的那种游戏。

lines.en: : I don’t put much thought into whether or not readers will understand something if it’s something I personally crafted to be obtuse and mystical.
lines.zh: : 如果某个东西是我特意做成晦涩而神秘的，我就不太会去想读者能不能理解它。

lines.en: : Because, like I said, coherence isn’t what’s important to me a lot of the time. And sometimes, I use the tools and characters (who are also tools) at my disposal to build something temporary.
lines.zh: : 因为就像我说的，很多时候连贯性对我来说并不重要。有时候，我会用手头的工具和角色（角色也是工具）去搭点临时性的东西。

lines.en: : Frequently, I like to wall the reader in and trap them in situations that appear {i}wrong{/i} because not only is that a cornerstone of the denpa genre, but it changes the way a reader interprets a scene.
lines.zh: : 我经常喜欢把读者围起来、困在显得{i}不对劲{/i}的处境里，因为这不仅是电波系的基石，还能改变读者解读一个场景的方式。

lines.en: : A person’s thought process changes when they’re stuck. And if I can effectively recreate that feeling each time I do something like Il Cervo, the reader’s mind will do the heavy lifting. Not me.
lines.zh: : 人被困住时思维过程会变。而如果我每次做《Il Cervo》这类东西时都能有效地重现那种感觉，那扛重活的就是读者的脑子。不是我。

lines.en: : So to hearken back to what I said moments ago, even if Lessons in Love is the type of game where I can making {i}anything{/i} fit in, there are a lot of things that aren’t supposed to.
lines.zh: : 所以回到我刚才说的：就算《Lessons in Love》是那种我能把{i}任何东西{/i}塞进去的游戏，也有很多东西本就不该被塞进去。

lines.en: : There are cracks {i}all{/i} over the place — and constant examples of different realities bleeding into one another.
lines.zh: : 到处都是裂缝——而且不断有不同现实互相渗入的例子。

lines.en: : You’re supposed to feel and notice those, and that’s not something I want to change about my style or work.
lines.zh: : 那些本就该被你感受到、注意到，而这不是我想在自己风格或作品里改变的东西。

lines.en: : Question seven — There are some clear misunderstandings in the interpretations of the stories between Ami, Kaori, and Sensei. Is it because they all see different meanings behind each of these analogies?
lines.zh: : 问题七——在 Ami、Kaori 和 Sensei 之间对彼此故事的解读里有一些明显的误解。是因为他们对每一个类比背后的含义都看到不同的东西吗？

lines.en: : Yes, precisely. Because again, this event is effectively a montage of different viewpoints clashing and compromising.
lines.zh: : 是的，正是如此。因为再说一次，这个事件实际上就是不同视角互相碰撞与妥协的蒙太奇。

lines.en: : Despite the misinterpretations though, there’s an underlying harmony in the coexistence of these characters in this moment.
lines.zh: : 不过尽管有这些误解，这些角色在这一刻的共处中仍有一种底层的和谐。

lines.en: : They don’t {i}need{/i} to understand one another. Just like the reader doesn’t need to understand the stories either.
lines.zh: : 他们{i}不需要{/i}互相理解。就像读者也不需要理解那些故事一样。

lines.en: : Fear is a very personal, customized emotion that varies entirely from one person to the next. All that matters is that you can sniff it out so you can figure out an escape plan. Or be hunted like the deer you/we are.
lines.zh: : 恐惧是一种极其私人、定制化的情绪，因人而异地完全不同。唯一重要的是你能嗅出它，从而想出一个逃跑计划。或者像你／我们这样的鹿一样被猎杀。

lines.en: : Question eight— What were your intentions with this event? What was intended to be the main take away for us?
lines.zh: : 问题八——你做这个事件的意图是什么？你想让我们得到的主要收获是什么？

lines.en: : I never expected anyone to {i}get{/i} Il Cervo — nor did I really want them to.
lines.zh: : 我从没指望有人能{i}看懂{/i}《Il Cervo》——我也并不真的想让他们看懂。

lines.en: : It’s the same way with all of the other similarly absurd and mysterious events of the game. The intention with these is to create a {i}feeling{/i} more than anything.
lines.zh: : 游戏里其他那些同样荒诞而神秘的事件也是如此。这些事件的意图，与其说是别的，不如说是制造一种{i}感受{/i}。

lines.en: : {size=-4}With Il Cervo, I wanted people to understand a reluctance to {i}move{/i} in regard to Kaori, Ami, and Akira — each for their own reasons. And I did this by creating a fake environment where progression was literally impossible.{/size}
lines.zh: : {size=-4}在《Il Cervo》里，我想让人理解 Kaori、Ami 和 Akira 那种不愿{i}前进{/i}的心态——各有各的理由。而我做到这一点的方式，是造出一个字面意义上无法推进的假环境。{/size}

lines.en: : I wanted the reader to feel unsettled, not scared. In fact, if anything, I wanted them to feel comfortable — and like the situation itself was normal despite nothing {i}within it{/i} making sense.
lines.zh: : 我想让读者感到不安，而不是害怕。其实真要说的话，我想让他们感到舒服——觉得这个处境本身很正常，哪怕它{i}里面{/i}没有任何东西说得通。

lines.en: : It was a very “Paprika”-esque move — wanting to portray a {i}dream{/i} in a way true to the way dreams are. And I feel like that was accomplished to a certain extent.
lines.zh: : 这是个很《红辣椒》式的做法——想以一种忠于梦本身样貌的方式描绘一场{i}梦{/i}。我觉得在某种程度上做到了。

lines.en: : But I also feel like it failed to a {i}different{/i} extent because it...was sort of fated to on a sheer conceptual basis.
lines.zh: : 但我也觉得它在{i}另一个{/i}层面上失败了，因为……纯粹从概念上讲，它某种程度上注定会失败。

lines.en: : It might not be perfect formulaically, but I don’t really think writing {i}has{/i} to be. And I think you can find flaws in anything if you look long enough or hard enough.
lines.zh: : 按公式来看它可能不完美，但我不觉得写作{i}必须{/i}完美。而且我觉得，只要你看得够久或够仔细，任何东西里都能找出瑕疵。

lines.en: : At the end of the day, Il Cervo is mostly just me letting my mind run wild as it leaks all over the place. Sort of like a deer who was just shot and is trying to get away. Just more {i}artsy.{/i}
lines.zh: : 说到底，《Il Cervo》大体上只是我让脑子放任狂奔、到处流淌。有点像一只刚被射中、正在努力逃走的鹿。只是更{i}文艺{/i}一点。

lines.en: : And while that may look messy to some, it makes me proud.
lines.zh: : 而虽然这在有些人看来可能很乱，它让我骄傲。

lines.en: : It reminds me of why I do this.
lines.zh: : 它让我想起我为什么做这些。

lines.en: : It reminds me that {i}we-{/i}
lines.zh: : 它让我想起{i}我们——{/i}

lines.en: scene black
: Are Il Cervo.
lines.zh: : 就是《Il Cervo》。
